justification: Display text on the DCP tab and one page-check rule

pre_impl.existing_data: condition and notes text in dcp_setback_controls, served by the structured-controls route
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: a council sentence containing 'NOT yet stored' would be dropped; the phrase is our marker only
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: every DCP tab render after deploy

falsifiable_check.command: jest __tests__/lib/dcp/public-condition.test.ts; pytest tests/test_page_integrity_checks_data.py; check.py on fresh captures
falsifiable_check.fails_when: an internal note sentence reaches the rendered DCP tab (C5 internal-note > 0) or a terrace row under dwelling houses stops being flagged (test_c4_winston_red)
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Live capture 2026-10-19 10:39 (origin/main): Mount Annan DCP tab shows '... are NOT yet stored.' (C5 internal-note=1); check.py gave C4=2 on Strathfield p.11 and Tempe p.8, both rows that cover dwelling houses. With this branch's check over the same capture: C4=0.

functions.name: publicCondition
functions.input: stored DCP row condition text from the structured-controls API
functions.output: the condition without our extraction notes, or null
functions.if_none: null or note-only text returns null and no condition is shown

values.if_missing: no own-type exemption for other project types; their rows are judged as before

break_it.scenario: a decimal like 6.5m inside the note's sentence
break_it.what_happens: splitting at every full stop would leave '6.' behind on the page
break_it.how: split only at '. ' followed by a capital

break_it.scenario: 'including deep soil zone' read as including other housing
break_it.what_happens: a terrace row would pass the check on a house project
break_it.how: 'including' must be followed by a housing type word

break_it.scenario: a row for terraces also says 'dwelling house' in passing
break_it.what_happens: the check would treat a terrace rule as a house rule
break_it.how: accepted: rows naming the house type are taken as covering it
